title: Chapter 138 — Pre-Delivery Communication
intro: Most delivery complaints start before the truck leaves the warehouse.

sections.title: The Confirmation Checklist
sections.content:
48 hours before delivery: confirm date and window by text and email. Not one or the other — both. Different customers check different channels.

Remind the customer to clear the path — remove rugs, move furniture, prop open doors. A 36-inch refrigerator through a hallway with a coat rack and a shoe bench is a scratched wall waiting to happen.

Confirm installation requirements are met — gas line on, water supply accessible, electrical outlet in place. These should have been verified at point of sale, but verify again. The customer who forgot to hire an electrician for the 240V outlet discovers it when the delivery crew is standing in their kitchen.

Set expectations on timing: 'The team will call 30 minutes before arrival. Delivery takes about 30-45 minutes including installation and haul-away. Someone 18 or older needs to be home.'

sections.title: Pre-Delivery Text Template
sections.content:
Text (send 48 hours before): 'Hi [name], your [appliance] delivery is confirmed for [day] between [window]. Please make sure the pathway is clear and your [gas/water/electric] connections are accessible. The team will call 30 min before arrival. Excited for you! — [Your name], [Store]'

Email (same day as text): Include everything from the text plus the model details, what is included (installation type, haul-away), and your direct contact info in case anything changes. Attach the original quote as a reference.

This communication reduces 'where is my delivery' calls by 80 percent and dramatically reduces day-of issues. Two minutes of your time prevents 20 minutes of complaint handling.

sections.title: What to Tell the Customer
sections.content:
Have them measure the delivery path — front door width, hallways, staircases, and any tight turns. A 36-inch fridge does not fit through a 32-inch doorway, and discovering this with the truck in the driveway is a nightmare for everyone.

Have them clear the area around the installation location — at least 3 feet on all sides. Have them confirm the old unit is emptied — food out of the fridge, clothes out of the washer. If they are handling disconnection themselves, confirm it is done.

For second-floor or basement deliveries, mention it explicitly: 'The team will bring it upstairs, but please clear the stairway completely.' Every detail you confirm before delivery is one less surprise on delivery day. Surprises on delivery day are never good.
